diff --git a/debian/patches/ubuntu-aa/lp2173698/0001-apparmor-Add-attach_disconnected-flag-to-passt-libvi.patch b/debian/patches/ubuntu-aa/lp2173698/0001-apparmor-Add-attach_disconnected-flag-to-passt-libvi.patch

--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/ubuntu-aa/lp2173698/0001-apparmor-Add-attach_disconnected-flag-to-passt-libvi.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+From 9ecbf2a65454704240170676b94b65866b352a34 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
+From: Hector Cao <hector.cao@canonical.com>
+Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 00:22:25 +0200
+Subject: [PATCH] apparmor: Add attach_disconnected flag to passt libvirt-qemu
+ subprofile
+
+From: Stefano Brivio <sbrivio@redhat.com>
+
+With passt commit 7bf1595c9242 ("isolation: Don't create our userns
+as nobody"), instead of a direct unshare() to detach the isolating
+user namespace, we now have a two-step process where we join the
+namespace by opening its procfs entry.
+
+After detaching the isolated namespace, AppArmor considers its procfs
+entry a disconnected object, so we don't have a way to refer to it
+unless we use the attach_disconnected flag in the relevant profile.
+
+For stand-alone passt(1) usage, this is taken care of in passt commit
+032f082ffad0 ("apparmor: Fixes for new user namespace detaching
+procedure"), but libvirt (as non-root) runs passt as a separate
+subprofile, and that's where we need to add that flag.
+
+Link: https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=1149683
+Signed-off-by: Stefano Brivio <sbrivio@redhat.com>
+Reviewed-by: Andrea Bolognani <abologna@redhat.com>
+
+Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+bug/2173698
+Origin: upstream, https://github.com/libvirt/libvirt/commit/9ecbf2a65454704240170676b94b65866b352a34
+
+---
+ src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu | 2 +-
+ 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)
+
+diff --git a/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu b/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu
+index 9bf572692b..4c6e5689c8 100644
+--- a/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu
++++ b/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu
+@@ -209,7 +209,7 @@
+   # support for passt network back-end
+   /usr/bin/passt Cx -> passt,
+ 
+-  profile passt {
++  profile passt flags=(attach_disconnected) {
+     /usr/bin/passt r,
+ 
+     signal (receive) set=("term") peer=/usr/sbin/libvirtd,
+-- 
+2.53.0
+
diff --git a/debian/patches/ubuntu-aa/lp2173698/0002-apparmor-Allow-passt-to-mmap-its-own-binary.patch b/debian/patches/ubuntu-aa/lp2173698/0002-apparmor-Allow-passt-to-mmap-its-own-binary.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bdd5d89
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/ubuntu-aa/lp2173698/0002-apparmor-Allow-passt-to-mmap-its-own-binary.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+From ee78b8a110e33aefd6680f2d68f24f81e1f402be Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
+From: Hector Cao <hector.cao@canonical.com>
+Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:55:16 +0100
+Subject: [PATCH 1/2] apparmor: Allow passt to mmap its own binary
+
+From: Hector Cao <hector.cao@canonical.com>
+
+The passt subprofile only grants read access to /usr/bin/passt. Once
+libvirt executes passt and it transitions into this subprofile, the
+binary also needs to be memory-mapped, which AppArmor mediates with
+the 'm' permission. Without it, passt is denied and the passt-backed
+interface cannot be set up:
+
+  apparmor="DENIED" operation="file_mmap" class="file"
+  profile="libvirt-794a597c-8a5d-436f-b13e-60c348b048f1"
+  name="/usr/bin/passt" pid=18206 comm="passt" requested_mask="rm"
+  denied_mask="rm" fsuid=64055 ouid=0
+
+Grant 'm' in addition to 'r' on /usr/bin/passt in the passt
+subprofile.
+
+Signed-off-by: Hector Cao <hector.cao@canonical.com>
+
+Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+bug/2173698
+Forwarded: https://lists.libvirt.org/archives/list/devel@lists.libvirt.org/thread/4P5SZPCCGGUIVYTBPTDD6EG3WJQO3BJ7/
+---
+ src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu | 2 +-
+ 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)
+
+diff --git a/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu b/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu
+index 4c6e5689c8..c977424023 100644
+--- a/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu
++++ b/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu
+@@ -210,7 +210,7 @@
+   /usr/bin/passt Cx -> passt,
+ 
+   profile passt flags=(attach_disconnected) {
+-    /usr/bin/passt r,
++    /usr/bin/passt rm,
+ 
+     signal (receive) set=("term") peer=/usr/sbin/libvirtd,
+     signal (receive) set=("term") peer=libvirtd,
+-- 
+2.53.0
+
diff --git a/debian/patches/ubuntu-aa/lp2173698/0003-apparmor-Allow-QEMU-to-access-the-passt-socket.patch b/debian/patches/ubuntu-aa/lp2173698/0003-apparmor-Allow-QEMU-to-access-the-passt-socket.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..18d528e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/ubuntu-aa/lp2173698/0003-apparmor-Allow-QEMU-to-access-the-passt-socket.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+From 0252425e899e3f2ca1c6a52a12a520693c7bdd8a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
+From: Hector Cao <hector.cao@canonical.com>
+Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 22:34:02 +0100
+Subject: [PATCH 2/2] apparmor: Allow QEMU to access the passt socket
+
+From: Hector Cao <hector.cao@canonical.com>
+
+For network device with <backend type='passt'/>, QEMU VM needs
+to connect to the unix socket created by passt (the socket path
+is created at qemuPasstCreateSocketPath()). The passt subprofile
+allows passt itself to create the socket, but the libvirt-qemu
+profile does not allow QEMU to connect to it, resulting in:
+
+  apparmor="DENIED" operation="connect" class="file"
+  profile="libvirt-d0132c94-8f89-4117-b668-9bfbb2902a0a"
+  name="/run/libvirt/qemu/passt/5-ubuntu-cloud-vm-pass-net0.socket"
+  pid=6995 comm="io-task-worker" requested_mask="wr" denied_mask="wr"
+  fsuid=64055 ouid=64055
+
+Signed-off-by: Hector Cao <hector.cao@canonical.com>
+
+Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+bug/2173698
+Forwarded: https://lists.libvirt.org/archives/list/devel@lists.libvirt.org/thread/4P5SZPCCGGUIVYTBPTDD6EG3WJQO3BJ7/
+---
+ src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu | 1 +
+ 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)
+
+diff --git a/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu b/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu
+index c977424023..5e70b5daa1 100644
+--- a/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu
++++ b/src/security/apparmor/libvirt-qemu
+@@ -208,6 +208,7 @@
+ 
+   # support for passt network back-end
+   /usr/bin/passt Cx -> passt,
++  /run/libvirt/qemu/passt/*.socket rw,
+ 
+   profile passt flags=(attach_disconnected) {
+     /usr/bin/passt rm,
+-- 
+2.53.0
+
diff --git a/debian/patches/ubuntu/lp2168017-node_device_udev-Don-t-hold-the-object-lock.patch b/debian/patches/ubuntu/lp2168017-node_device_udev-Don-t-hold-the-object-lock.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..2aa8fa3
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/ubuntu/lp2168017-node_device_udev-Don-t-hold-the-object-lock.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+From 0c053ffd2c44ef0820886ab79c1f812775b2cd15 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
+From: Yifan Li <yifan2.li@intel.com>
+Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 18:27:08 +0800
+Subject: [PATCH] node_device_udev: Don't hold the object lock while joining
+ the udev thread
+
+We found libvirt has a race condition bug and it causes systemd
+timeout during system shutdown. This issue does not exist on
+libvirt 10.0.0 with Ubuntu 24.04 but found in Ubuntu 26.04 which
+uses libvirt 12.0.0.
+
+nodeStateShutdownWait() joins the udev event thread while holding
+@priv's object lock:
+
+    VIR_WITH_OBJECT_LOCK_GUARD(priv) {
+        if (priv->udevThread)
+            virThreadJoin(priv->udevThread);
+    }
+
+but udevEventHandleThread() needs that same lock to make progress. Its
+only clean exit path is
+
+    VIR_WITH_OBJECT_LOCK_GUARD(priv) {
+        while (!priv->udevDataReady && !priv->udevThreadQuit) {
+            if (virCondWait(&priv->udevThreadCond, &priv->parent.lock))
+                ...
+        }
+        if (priv->udevThreadQuit)
+            return;
+
+so the thread has to re-acquire the lock - either on return from
+virCondWait() or to re-enter the guard at the top of its loop - before
+it can observe @priv->udevThreadQuit and return.
+
+nodeStateShutdownPrepare() sets udevThreadQuit, signals the condition
+and drops the lock. Which thread grabs the lock next then decides the
+outcome:
+
+  - the udev thread wins: it sees udevThreadQuit, returns, and the
+    subsequent join completes immediately.
+  - nodeStateShutdownWait() wins: it takes the lock and blocks in
+    virThreadJoin(), so the udev thread can never re-acquire the lock,
+    never observes udevThreadQuit and never returns. Both threads are
+    then stuck for good.
+
+Holding the lock across the join serves no purpose - udevThreadQuit has
+already been published by nodeStateShutdownPrepare(), @priv->udevThread
+is only assigned in nodeStateInitialize() and released by
+udevEventDataDispose(), and the udev thread holds a reference to @priv.
+Join outside the lock guard instead, which also restores the ordering
+nodeStateCleanup() used before commit e89d39f5b8f3 ("node_device_udev:
+Introduce and use `stateShutdownPrepare` and `stateShutdownWait`"):
+signal under the lock, release it, then join.
+
+Fixes: e89d39f5b8f30f0b3284ed2bd71cee1a8a3d707d
+Signed-off-by: Yifan Li <yifan2.li@intel.com>
+Signed-off-by: Jianfeng Gao <jianfeng.gao@intel.com>
+Signed-off-by: Lili Li <lili.li@intel.com>
+Reviewed-by: Michal Privoznik <mprivozn@redhat.com>
+
+Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+bug/2168017
+Origin: upstream, https://gitlab.com/libvirt/libvirt/-/commit/0c053ffd2c44ef0820886ab79c1f812775b2cd15
+---
+ src/node_device/node_device_udev.c | 15 +++++++++++----
+ 1 file changed, 11 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
+
+diff --git a/src/node_device/node_device_udev.c b/src/node_device/node_device_udev.c
+index 104433fb88..ac9be10382 100644
+--- a/src/node_device/node_device_udev.c
++++ b/src/node_device/node_device_udev.c
+@@ -2482,10 +2482,17 @@ nodeStateShutdownWait(void)
+     if (!priv)
+         return 0;
+ 
+-    VIR_WITH_OBJECT_LOCK_GUARD(priv) {
+-        if (priv->udevThread)
+-            virThreadJoin(priv->udevThread);
+-    }
++    /* Do not hold @priv's lock while joining the udev thread.
++     * udevEventHandleThread() must acquire that very lock in order to
++     * observe @priv->udevThreadQuit - already set by
++     * nodeStateShutdownPrepare() - and return. Joining while holding the
++     * lock therefore deadlocks the two threads against each other.
++     *
++     * @priv->udevThread is only ever assigned in nodeStateInitialize() and
++     * released by udevEventDataDispose(), and the udev thread holds a
++     * reference to @priv, so accessing it here without the lock is safe. */
++    if (priv->udevThread)
++        virThreadJoin(priv->udevThread);
+ 
+     if (priv->workerPool)
+         virThreadPoolDrain(priv->workerPool);
+-- 
+2.43.0
+
